$comment: GENERATED by `npm run routes:emit` from inbound/src/routes.ts. Do not edit by hand:
inbound/route-table.test.ts fails when this file and the source disagree.
The worker's HTTP route table (#417/#449). One place where a route, its method,
and the token scope it demands are written down for every seam: the worker
validates itself against it (inbound/route-contract.test.ts drives the REAL
handleApi), and each client asserts the paths it emits are paths the worker
serves. Before this, every suite mocked its own idea of the worker, which is how
the published clients drifted a feature generation behind with green tests.
Adding a route means adding a row to inbound/src/routes.ts and re-emitting.
scope: what requiredScope() demands; null means the route is not behind the bearer
scope gate at all, and `auth` says what guards it instead.
match: exact = the whole path; prefix = this path plus anything under it.

routes.note: JSON uptime probe only; do not probe GET / for health
HTML product landing (links to /webmail); not the health JSON
SEO robots + Sitemap pointer; served only on the posternonline.com zone (apex or any subdomain), 404 elsewhere so a self-hosted deploy never advertises the demo
SEO sitemap for demo landing + webmail; same posternonline.com zone gate as robots
the single-page human door; the page then calls the API with its own session
the relay and the IMAP door send `secret`, as CONTRACT.md 9 documents (#829); precred-body-contract.test.ts pins the declared body to what the handler reads

first run (#791, contract 1.10.7): armed only when WEBMAIL_AUTH_BACKEND is explicitly native AND the POSTERN_SETUP_TOKEN secret is set AND the account table is EMPTY; atomic; 409 E_SETUP_COMPLETE once any user exists; 404 when not armed
self-service change password (#790, contract 1.10.5): cookie session + CSRF only, a Bearer is refused; throttled on the sign-in keys; rotates this session and ends the others
inbound mail ingestion, gated by POSTERN_TRANSPORT_TOKEN, never a mailbox token
attachments are base64 over JSON (#70); forwardMessageId quotes a stored message, recipients stay caller-selected
back-compat alias of /api/send: the same handler, so deliberately the same list
mode reply|replyAll derives the original recipients server-side (#363)
`for` writes a per-recipient override; under a session it must be the session identity (#410)
mailbox archive|trash|junk, or null to restore the direction-default view

list/create/update/delete/send plus draft attachments. Identity-owned: a static operator token gets E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED. PUT on an EXISTING draft requires its current updatedAt; an absent one is a conflict too, so an edit is read-modify-write
the door has no ambient identity, so it asserts the already-authenticated one on every call
folder sent|archive|trash|junk; rawMime is base64, refused 413 E_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE (before parse) past 22 MiB decoded (#493)

role membership is single-sourced on the Worker (#438): the door reads this map per login instead of parsing its own mirror var. Same projection as the operator /api/roles, gated on the least-privilege door token
the bare prefix (no username) is deliberately NOT claimed, matching the original regex
human accounts (#790, contract 1.10.4): one keyset page ordered by username; never carries a hash
create only, never overwrites (409 E_CONFLICT); a generated password is returned once
operator reset: ends the user's sessions and clears the account lockout
disable or a from change ends the user's sessions
runtime agent identities (#801): one keyset page ordered by createdAt; never carries a token or its hash; active only unless includeRevoked=1. Audited (identity.list)

scopes from read|send|organize; anything else (delete, imap, admin, both, a typo) is 400, never stripped. Returns the token ONCE (201); it is never retrievable again and only its sha256 is stored. Authenticates on the next request, no deploy. Audited (identity.mint)
the next request with its token is 401; no deploy. Idempotent; the row is kept with revokedAt and its id is never reused. Audited (identity.revoke)
#740 S1: one keyset page ordered by createdAt; active only unless includeRevoked=1; grantee= (an idn_ id) and address= filter. Audited (delegation.list)

#740 S1: granteeId must be a LIVE agent identity (400 E_GRANTEE_INVALID otherwise, checked in the same statement as the insert); powers from read|organize|quote|send_as, anything else 400, and every power implies read (the stored set always carries it); address on the deploy domain and not the grantee's own; one active grant per (grantee, address), else 409 E_CONFLICT. No behaviour change in S1. Audited (delegation.grant)
#740 S1: idempotent; the row is kept with revokedAt and its id is never reused. Audited (delegation.revoke)
#854 M1: copy agent identities, human users and the static slots into the principal tables. Idempotent and convergent; store only, nothing authorizes from it yet. Audited (principals.backfill)
the audit log (#801), newest first: actor, action, target, outcome, detail. Refusals are recorded too
#507 refill projected_size after a PROJECTION_VERSION bump (idempotent; dryRun writes nothing); #520 countOnly returns { total, atCurrent, notCurrent } with no paging
the role map is operator config (#425): who is on which queue is a deployment fact, not a mailbox view, so a read token cannot see it
read-only report, gated admin because it spans the whole estate
not the /attachments/ sub-path

the caller identity and the scope the SERVER imposes on its reads (#650): bound identity or null, the same identityScope projection /api/messages and /api/search emit, the role queues that identity may also read via to=, and the capability set the gate honours (derived by asking authorize() per scope, never a second list). Takes no parameters, so it reports the scope a BARE read would get

lens needs a viewer and refuses direction (#403); under a session to= filters INSIDE the account boundary (#422); seenFor moves only the read-state projection key (#404); fields= projects the response to named summary keys and REFUSES an unknown one (#646); after=/before= are INCLUSIVE at BOTH ends, ISO-8601 date or timestamp, a bare date covering its whole named day, and a bogus value is refused not applied (#647); countOnly=1 answers { total } for the SAME filters and the SAME access scope with no items and no cursor, and is REFUSED alongside limit/cursor/fields because all three describe rows a count does not return (#648, mirroring admin-reproject's countOnly from #520)

mode fts|substr|semantic|hybrid; field pairs with substr; the view filters mirror messages-list exactly because they share one builder. Mind the pair: field (SINGULAR) selects the substr COLUMN MATCHED, fields (PLURAL, #646) selects the summary keys RETURNED on hit.message; both are validated strictly. after=/before= are the SAME inclusive, canonicalized, strictly-refused bounds messages-list uses (#647); they were unvalidated here until then. cursor is the (date, id) keyset on fts and substr; on semantic and hybrid it is REFUSED with E_VALIDATION_ERROR, never accepted and dropped, because those modes are score-ranked and have no continuation (#803)
a bound identity wins; an unbound BYO token must name viewer= or to=, never an estate dump
to= scopes the unread counts; a bound identity wins over it server-side
per-user Apple profile; carries NO password
single message and its /attachments/{i} sub-route

bounded and keyset-paginated (#649): it used to select EVERY message in the thread, bodies included, with no LIMIT and no cursor. Oldest first, so the keyset reads FORWARD through the same (date, id) tuple the other read routes use. Default 20, lower than the summary default because a thread row carries full bodies; max 200. `cursor: null` is the POSITIVE claim that this is the whole thread, so a non-null cursor means first page, not thread
